content.value_statement: Teams lose time when project docs lack structure. This skill provides ready templates for READMEs, API docs, changelogs, ADRs, and AI-friendly docs.
actual_capabilities: Provides a priority-ordered README structure with quick start, features, configuration, documentation, and license sections.
Defines a per-endpoint API documentation template with purpose, parameters, responses, and examples.
Shows a JSDoc and TSDoc comment template with parameters, return values, errors, and examples.
Includes a changelog structure based on added, changed, and fixed sections.
Provides an ADR template with status, context, decision, and consequences.
Outlines llms.txt and RAG-ready documentation practices for AI agents.
limitations: Does not inspect repositories or verify that documentation matches source code.
Does not generate complete product-specific examples without user input.
Does not replace legal, compliance, or domain expert review.
Does not enforce style guides or publish documentation automatically.

use_cases.title: Standardize Engineering Docs
use_cases.description: Create a shared documentation baseline for new services, libraries, or internal tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare API References
use_cases.description: Structure endpoint documentation before handoff to developers, writers, or customer support teams.

use_cases.title: Improve Open Source Projects
use_cases.description: Add predictable README, changelog, ADR, and AI-facing documentation sections for contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the documentation-templates skill to draft a README for this project: [project summary]. Include quick start, features, configuration, documentation, and license.

prompt_templates.title: Document an API Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the API documentation template for this endpoint: [method and path]. Include purpose, parameters, responses, and an example description.

prompt_templates.title: Write an ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ADR template to document this decision: [decision]. Include status, context, decision, and consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Build AI-Friendly Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation plan for [project]. Include README structure, code comment guidance, changelog sections, ADRs, llms.txt, and RAG-ready sections.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for README guidance for a new library.
output: A README outline with title, purpose, quick start, features, configuration, documentation links, and license.
Brief placeholders for each section so the maintainer can fill project details.

output_examples.input: A team needs to record a storage decision.
output_examples.output: An ADR draft with status, context, decision, consequences, and trade-offs in plain language.

output_examples.input: A product team needs endpoint documentation.
output_examples.output: An endpoint document outline with path, purpose, parameter table, response cases, and example request notes.

best_practices: Start with the smallest useful document, then add details as readers ask repeated questions.
Replace placeholders with project-specific names, commands, endpoints, and constraints before publishing.
Keep changelogs, ADRs, and AI-facing files synchronized with major product changes.
anti_patterns: Adding comments that repeat obvious code behavior.
Treating an ADR as final when the decision is still unresolved.

faq.question: Does this skill generate full documentation automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structure and starter wording. You still need project-specific details, examples, and validation.

faq.question: Can it write API reference pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives a per-endpoint structure for purpose, parameters, responses, and examples.

faq.question: Does it support AI-friendly documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes llms.txt guidance and RAG-ready structure principles.

faq.question: Is it limited to software projects?
faq.answer: It is best for software and technical product documentation, but templates can adapt to adjacent technical work.

faq.question: Does it run commands or inspect my repository?
faq.answer: No. The skill content is guidance only. Any repository review must be requested separately.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
